title: Torsades de pointes (long QT)
summary: In long QT, early afterdepolarisations trigger a polymorphic VT whose complexes twist about the baseline.
source: Slides 49 (triggered activity, EAD), 80-82 (polymorphic VT, torsades, long QT)

events.label: Prolonged repolarisation
events.caption: In long QT syndrome ventricular repolarisation is prolonged. During the plateau, calcium re-enters and the cell membrane oscillates: an early afterdepolarisation (EAD).

events.label: Triggered beat
events.caption: An EAD reaches threshold and fires an extra beat. This is triggered activity, not a circuit: the focus changes from beat to beat.
events.ecg: A premature wide complex, often after a long pause.

events.label: Moving focus
events.caption: Each new beat is triggered from a different site. The ventricles are activated in a different order every time, so the QRS changes shape (polymorphic).
events.ecg: The complexes change in size and direction: the twisting of the points.

events.label: Twisting
events.caption: The wide complexes wax and wane around the baseline. Hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, bradycardia and many drugs can cause it, as can genetic long QT syndromes.
events.ecg: A twisting, polymorphic wide-complex tachycardia. It may stop by itself or degenerate to VF.

teaching_points: Triggered activity: early afterdepolarisations (phase 2-3) in long QT, delayed afterdepolarisations (phase 4) in digoxin toxicity and CPVT (slide 49).
Torsades de pointes is a polymorphic VT in the setting of a long QT interval (slides 80-82).
Causes: congenital long QT syndromes, hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, drugs and bradycardia (slide 82).
This illustration shows the ventricular activation sequence only; the cellular mechanism is not simulated.
